To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security

to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.

email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.

a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each

each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline view

The package is not "fair and balanced." Taken together, three things would leave Wattlebridge with little real warranty protection:

- general disclosure of the whole data room and public records,
- a constructive-knowledge bar (cl 8.3), and
- limitations that apply to "all Claims of any nature."

The package also leaves the Riverlark debt, the Bluefen consent, the Ironquay IP, the bonuses and the privacy incident as Buyer risk. The cover note also describes several issues more favourably than the Seller's own Disclosure Letter does:

| Topic | Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "Addressed" | Consent not obtained; cl 11.3 conditions not shown as satisfied (§2) |
| Riverlark | Release after Completion | Not repaid; no discharge of security (§3) |
| Ironquay | Indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt or assignment; title to SOW3 materials depends on payment (§4) |
| DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification obligations all unknown (§6) |

The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. Today is 6 November 2026, so it is about six weeks stale. We need a refreshed position on every open item.

---

## Part A: Structural issues (warranty and limitation framework)

### 1. Fundamental warranties subject to the general cap and time limit. **Reject.**
- Title and capacity are the core of a share purchase. Capping them at AUD 4.8m (20%) means that if title fails, we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m.
- **Position:**
  - Title, capacity and authority warranties capped at 100% of the price (plus costs).
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - Time limit of at least 6 years. Consider aligning with NSW limitation periods (6 years in contract, 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed). If you choose the deed route, confirm execution formalities.
  - Not subject to cl 8.3 or general disclosure.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to shift this risk.

### 2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 13 / 20.5). **Reject.**
- As drafted, the AUD 4.8m cap, the thresholds and the 18-month limit would also catch:
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses),
  - the tax indemnity,
  - price adjustment and debt-free/cash-free mechanics,
  - breach of pre-Completion covenants, and
  - arguably fraud.
- The default in cl 12.3 ("applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") reverses the burden onto us to carve everything out. We should flip it so limitations apply **only to Warranty Claims** (other than fundamental and tax warranties).
- **Express carve-outs** from all limitations, the exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers and advisers;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax;
  - specific indemnities;
  - covenants;
  - completion and price mechanics.
- **Non-reliance:** keep a fraud carve-out. Note that Australian Consumer Law s18 claims cannot simply be contracted out of, but a non-reliance clause can undermine the causation element. We should not concede a broad clause.

### 3. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). **Reject.**
- Barring claims for anything "discoverable from the data room or public records," and imputing advisers' knowledge, is a very broad anti-sandbagging clause. Combined with general disclosure, it would neutralise most warranties. It would also arguably bar claims on the very issues we have flagged (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006).
- **Position (in order of preference):**
  1. Express pro-sandbagging: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce claims.
  2. Fallback: only matters **Fairly Disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter qualify warranties. Nothing else, including Buyer knowledge, does.
- Specific indemnities must apply **regardless** of disclosure or knowledge. That is their purpose.

### 4. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2, Schedule 7). **Reject or narrow heavily.**
- Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable" records is too broad.
- **Position:**
  - Disclosures qualify warranties only where **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial effect.
  - Data room disclosure limited to documents in an agreed, indexed USB or data room copy, and only to the extent fairly disclosed.
  - Public records limited to specified searches (ASIC, PPSR, court) of the Company on specified dates.
  - Document references like "Read together" in §8 are not adequate disclosure.
- **§1.4 (no admissions):** acceptable only if it states that it does not limit the Buyer's rights or reduce the effect of any specific indemnity.
- **§11 (reservation):** this confirms the Seller is giving facts, not comfort. That supports our position that the open items must be dealt with in the SPA, not accepted as disclosed.

### 5. Disclosure update and bring-down. **New point.**
- The SPA must provide:
  - no updating disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion without Buyer consent;
  - a Buyer termination right if a new matter arises that would be a material breach; and
  - a refreshed Disclosure Letter as at signing, given the date gap above.

### 6. Cap, thresholds and time limit (cl 12.1 / 12.2 / 12.3)
These terms are within the range of market outcomes, but at the Seller-favourable end.
- **Cap:** 20% (AUD 4.8m) is arguable for general warranties only once fundamentals, tax and indemnities are carved out. Open at 40–50%, with 30% a reasonable landing point. If W&I insurance is used, cap Seller recourse at the retention.
- **Basket:** AUD 250k (about 1.04%) operating as a **deductible** is Seller-friendly.
  - Push for a **tipping basket**: once exceeded, recovery from dollar one.
  - Push the amount to around 0.5% (AUD 120k).
  - Related claims from the same facts should **aggregate** for both the de minimis and the basket. Otherwise items like the three Sandbar renewals could be argued separately.
- **De minimis:** AUD 25k is acceptable, subject to aggregation of related claims.
- **Time limit:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, to capture a full audit cycle.
  - Tax: the relevant ATO amendment period plus 6 months, and unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - Fundamental warranties: per item 1.

### 7. Covenant strength and recoverability
- Harbourglass Ventures is a ventures vehicle that may distribute proceeds soon after Completion.
- **Ask for:**
  - an escrow or retention, for example 10% (AUD 2.4m) for 18–24 months, plus a separate escrow for the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, tax); and/or
  - a creditworthy guarantor; or
  - W&I insurance with Seller backstop for excluded matters.
- Known issues are typically excluded from W&I cover, so the specific indemnities still need Seller backing.

---

## Part B: Transaction-specific issues

### 8. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m), cl 2 / 7. **Critical. Reject "release after Completion."**
- A debt-free/cash-free deal at AUD 24m means this debt must be repaid at Completion from the price.
- The facility has a change-control clause (cl 8.1). Completing without a payout risks an event of default or acceleration against a Company we then own.
- A post-Completion release would leave security over Company assets, and possibly over the shares if there is a share mortgage. That also goes to title.
- **Position:**
  - Riverlark payout letter (with daily interest and break costs) as a Completion deliverable.
  - Repayment shown as a line in the funds flow, deducted from the price.
  - Signed deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements or discharge undertakings, and the return of title documents, all delivered at Completion.
  - Break costs, fees and accrued interest treated as Debt.
  - Confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the shares held by Harbourglass.

### 9. Bluefen consent (about 30% of revenue, about AUD 3.6m in FY26), cl 3 / 6.3. **Critical.**
- The Seller's position has three problems:
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is weak.
  - "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions.
  - It would allow a conditional consent, or one with amended commercial terms, to satisfy the condition.
- **Position:**
  - **Condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only (waivable only by the Buyer):** an unconditional written consent from Bluefen to the change of control.
    - The form must be reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer.
    - There must be evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
    - The consent must not amend pricing, term or termination rights.
  - Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours). The Seller bears the costs.
  - The Buyer has rights to review and comment on correspondence with Bluefen.
  - The Buyer has a termination right at the long-stop date.
- Consider a price adjustment or specific protection if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces the contract within an agreed period after Completion.

### 10. Ironquay / SOW3 IP, cl 11.1. **Reject "adequate."**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k remains open (DD-010).
- On the data room as it stands, the Company may not own the SOW3 materials. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk, which is loss of the IP or infringement claims.
- **Position:**
  - **Before Completion:** the outstanding SOW3 fees are paid at the Seller's cost (or treated as Debt). Evidence of cleared payment, written confirmation from Ironquay that all SOW3 fees are paid, and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** (with moral rights consents where relevant) are Completion deliverables.
  - **Specific indemnity** covering any loss from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption. The indemnity sits outside the cap, thresholds, knowledge and disclosure provisions, with its own longer time limit.
- The IP warranties should not be qualified by the Ironquay disclosure.

### 11. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k) omitted from the funds flow. **Reject "a matter for the Seller."**
- These bonuses are triggered by the transaction and become Company liabilities. Leaving them out of the funds flow inflates equity value.
- On-costs may also apply and the disclosure does not address them: PAYG withholding, possibly superannuation depending on characterisation, NSW payroll tax and workers compensation. The all-in cost could plausibly be around AUD 450–500k. Accounting or tax advisers should confirm the figure.
- **Position:**
  - Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from the price, paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion and funded by the Seller.
  - Add an indemnity for any shortfall or any related claims, including those under the continued-employment conditions.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (about 1,240 records). **Reject "not material."**
- The incident involved personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external recipient.
- As at 22 September, the Seller had not established whether the file was accessed, the scope of the incident, or whether notification is required.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days. Depending on when the Company became aware of the incident, that window may already have passed. The penalty regime and enforcement risk have also increased under recent amendments.
- Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen, may carry their own breach notification obligations.
- **Position:**
  - **Immediate information request:** the incident timeline (including the date of awareness), the forensic report, any recall or deletion confirmation from the recipient, the NDB assessment, any OAIC or customer notifications, and insurer notification.
  - **Specific indemnity** for all losses from the incident: regulatory, customer, remediation, notification, legal, and contractual claims including from Bluefen. The indemnity sits outside the general limitations, knowledge and disclosure provisions, and is backed by escrow.
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Seller must cause the Company to complete the assessment and make any required notifications properly. The Buyer has consultation rights.
  - Consider making a satisfactory incident report a CP, depending on what the update shows.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k). **Do not accept "ordinary course" on the Seller's say-so.**
- The disclosure describes three *related* renewals that should be "read together," but does not say whether each is ordinary course, terminable, accrued or unavoidable.
- Three related commitments of equal value warrant scrutiny on several fronts:
  - **Timing:** were they entered during the conduct-of-business period?
  - **Related party:** is any counterparty connected to the Seller?
  - **Value:** does the price reflect market terms?
  - **Approval:** were they properly authorised?
- **Ask for:** the contracts, dates, approvals, termination rights and accounting treatment.
- **Position:**
  - Renewals entered after the agreed reference date, or outside the ordinary course, require Buyer consent. Otherwise the Seller arranges termination at its cost, or the committed amounts are treated as Debt.
  - Add a related-party warranty.
  - Aggregate related claims for threshold purposes (see item 6).

### 14. Tax. **Reject "settled under the general regime."**
- **Position:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and stamp duty, and tax arising from the bonuses and the transaction.
  - Capped at the price.
  - Time limit tied to the amendment periods plus a buffer.
  - Not subject to the basket, de minimis, knowledge or general disclosure.
  - Conduct-of-claims provisions.
- The IP warranties likewise sit outside any disclosure of the Ironquay issue (see item 10).

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012). **Insufficient on its own.**
- The share register is only prima facie evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter (§10) itself flags that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Our verification:**
  - ASIC current and historical company extracts.
  - The constitution, any shareholders' agreement and any pre-emption waivers.
  - Share issue and transfer history.
  - PPSR searches against both the Company and Harbourglass.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertible notes, SAFEs, ESOP awards or other rights to shares.
- **Completion deliverables:** share certificates, signed transfers, waivers of pre-emption rights, and releases of any security over the shares.
- **Warranties:** full title and capitalisation warranties as fundamental warranties (see item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). Lower risk, but tidy up.
- **Lease:** make giving the required notice to the landlord a Seller pre-Completion obligation or a Completion deliverable. Obtain a copy of the notice.
- **Mossvale:** the restriction applies to assignment, not change of control. Obtain a warranty that, apart from Bluefen and Riverlark, no Material Contract contains a change-of-control or similar trigger. We will also verify this in our own review of DD-009.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Our position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Riverlark AUD 3.2m** | Repay at Completion from the price; payout letter and releases (including PPSR discharges) are Completion deliverables. No post-Completion release. |
| 2 | **Bluefen consent** (30% of revenue) | Buyer-only CP: unconditional consent with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and no adverse terms. All reasonable endeavours; long-stop walk right. |
| 3 | **Limitations scope** (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/13/20.5) | Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, covenants and price mechanics. |
| 4 | **Buyer knowledge (8.3) and general disclosure** | Reject constructive knowledge; pro-sandbagging. Only Fair Disclosure in the letter qualifies warranties; data room and public record disclosure narrowed. |
| 5 | **Fundamental warranties** | Capped at 100% of price, at least 6 years, no thresholds; full title verification and deliverables. |
| 6 | **DD-006 privacy incident** | Urgent update request; specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity with escrow; NDB compliance covenant; possible CP. |
| 7 | **Ironquay SOW3 IP** | Pay outstanding fees at Seller cost before Completion; confirmatory assignment as a deliverable; broad specific IP indemnity outside limitations. |
| 8 | **Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs** | Treat as Transaction Costs/Debt, deducted from price; indemnity for shortfall. |
| 9 | **Tax** | Standalone tax indemnity, capped at price, tied to amendment periods. |
| 10 | **Sandbar AUD 330k** | Full information; Buyer consent requirement or Debt treatment; related-party warranty; aggregation of related claims. |
| 11 | **Cap / basket / time** | Cap 30–50%; tipping basket around AUD 120k; aggregate related claims; 24 months general. |
| 12 | **Recoverability** | Escrow or retention (around 10%) plus specific-indemnity escrow, or guarantor / W&I with Seller backstop. |
| 13 | **Bring-down** | Refreshed Disclosure Letter at signing; no curative updates; termination right for material new matters. |
| 14 | **Lease / Mossvale** | Lease notice as Seller deliverable; no-other-change-of-control warranty. |

**Next steps:**
1. Send an information request covering DD-006, Sandbar, the Ironquay payment status, the Riverlark payout figure and the Bluefen correspondence.
2. Prepare the SPA mark-up and a revised funds flow showing deductions for the Riverlark repayment and the bonuses and on-costs.
3. Ask tax and accounting advisers to confirm the bonus on-costs and the tax indemnity periods.
4. Decide on W&I insurance early, as it affects positions on the cap and escrow.

*Caveat:* this review is based only on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents or the full SPA text. Statutory points (NDB timing, limitation periods, payroll tax and super treatment) should be confirmed by the responsible Australian practitioners before positions are finalised.

  - Related claims from the same facts should **aggregate** for both the de minimis and the basket. Otherwise items like the three Sandbar renewals could be argued separately.
- **De minimis:** AUD 25k is acceptable, subject to aggregation of related claims.
- **Time limit:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, to capture a full audit cycle.
  - Tax: the relevant ATO amendment period plus 6 months, and unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - Fundamental warranties: per item 1.

### 7. Covenant strength and recoverability
- Harbourglass Ventures is a ventures vehicle that may distribute proceeds soon after Completion.
- **Ask for:**
  - an escrow or retention, for example 10% (AUD 2.4m) for 18–24 months, plus a separate escrow for the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, tax); and/or
  - a creditworthy guarantor; or
  - W&I insurance with Seller backstop for excluded matters.
- Known issues are typically excluded from W&I cover, so the specific indemnities still need Seller backing.

## Part B: Transaction-specific issues

### 8. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m), cl 2 / 7. **Critical. Reject "release after Completion."**
- A debt-free/cash-free deal at AUD 24m means this debt must be repaid at Completion from the price.
- The facility has a change-control clause (cl 8.1). Completing without a payout risks an event of default or acceleration against a Company we then own.
- A post-Completion release would leave security over Company assets, and possibly over the shares if there is a share mortgage. That also goes to title.
- **Position:**
  - Riverlark payout letter (with daily interest and break costs) as a Completion deliverable.
  - Repayment shown as a line in the funds flow, deducted from the price.
  - Signed deeds of release, PPSR financing change statements or discharge undertakings, and the return of title documents, all delivered at Completion.
  - Break costs, fees and accrued interest treated as Debt.
  - Confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the shares held by Harbourglass.

### 9. Bluefen consent (about 30% of revenue, about AUD 3.6m in FY26), cl 3 / 6.3. **Critical.**
- The Seller's position has three problems:
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is weak.
  - "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions.
  - It would allow a conditional consent, or one with amended commercial terms, to satisfy the condition.
- **Position:**
  - **Condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only (waivable only by the Buyer):** an unconditional written consent from Bluefen to the change of control.
    - The form must be reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer.
    - There must be evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
    - The consent must not amend pricing, term or termination rights.
  - Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours). The Seller bears the costs.
  - The Buyer has rights to review and comment on correspondence with Bluefen.
  - The Buyer has a termination right at the long-stop date.
- Consider a price adjustment or specific protection if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces the contract within an agreed period after Completion.

### 10. Ironquay / SOW3 IP, cl 11.1. **Reject "adequate."**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k remains open (DD-010).
- On the data room as it stands, the Company may not own the SOW3 materials. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk, which is loss of the IP or infringement claims.
- **Position:**
  - **Before Completion:** the outstanding SOW3 fees are paid at the Seller's cost (or treated as Debt). Evidence of cleared payment, written confirmation from Ironquay that all SOW3 fees are paid, and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** (with moral rights consents where relevant) are Completion deliverables.
  - **Specific indemnity** covering any loss from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption. The indemnity sits outside the cap, thresholds, knowledge and disclosure provisions, with its own longer time limit.
- The IP warranties should not be qualified by the Ironquay disclosure.

### 11. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k) omitted from the funds flow. **Reject "a matter for the Seller."**
- These bonuses are triggered by the transaction and become Company liabilities. Leaving them out of the funds flow inflates equity value.
- On-costs may also apply and the disclosure does not address them: PAYG withholding, possibly superannuation depending on characterisation, NSW payroll tax and workers compensation. The all-in cost could plausibly be around AUD 450–500k. Accounting or tax advisers should confirm the figure.
- **Position:**
  - Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt**, deducted from the price, paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion and funded by the Seller.
  - Add an indemnity for any shortfall or any related claims, including those under the continued-employment conditions.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (about 1,240 records). **Reject "not material."**
- The incident involved personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external recipient.
- As at 22 September, the Seller had not established whether the file was accessed, the scope of the incident, or whether notification is required.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days. Depending on when the Company became aware of the incident, that window may already have passed. The penalty regime and enforcement risk have also increased under recent amendments.
- Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen, may carry their own breach notification obligations.
- **Position:**
  - **Immediate information request:** the incident timeline (including the date of awareness), the forensic report, any recall or deletion confirmation from the recipient, the NDB assessment, any OAIC or customer notifications, and insurer notification.
  - **Specific indemnity** for all losses from the incident: regulatory, customer, remediation, notification, legal, and contractual claims including from Bluefen. The indemnity sits outside the general limitations, knowledge and disclosure provisions, and is backed by escrow.
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Seller must cause the Company to complete the assessment and make any required notifications properly. The Buyer has consultation rights.
  - Consider making a satisfactory incident report a CP, depending on what the update shows.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k). **Do not accept "ordinary course" on the Seller's say-so.**
- The disclosure describes three *related* renewals that should be "read together," but does not say whether each is ordinary course, terminable, accrued or unavoidable.
- Three related commitments of equal value warrant scrutiny on several fronts:
  - **Timing:** were they entered during the conduct-of-business period?
  - **Related party:** is any counterparty connected to the Seller?
  - **Value:** does the price reflect market terms?
  - **Approval:** were they properly authorised?
- **Ask for:** the contracts, dates, approvals, termination rights and accounting treatment.
- **Position:**
  - Renewals entered after the agreed reference date, or outside the ordinary course, require Buyer consent. Otherwise the Seller arranges termination at its cost, or the committed amounts are treated as Debt.
  - Add a related-party warranty.
  - Aggregate related claims for threshold purposes (see item 6).

### 14. Tax. **Reject "settled under the general regime."**
- **Position:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and stamp duty, and tax arising from the bonuses and the transaction.
  - Capped at the price.
  - Time limit tied to the amendment periods plus a buffer.
  - Not subject to the basket, de minimis, knowledge or general disclosure.
  - Conduct-of-claims provisions.
- The IP warranties likewise sit outside any disclosure of the Ironquay issue (see item 10).

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012). **Insufficient on its own.**
- The share register is only prima facie evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter (§10) itself flags that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Our verification:**
  - ASIC current and historical company extracts.
  - The constitution, any shareholders' agreement and any pre-emption waivers.
  - Share issue and transfer history.
  - PPSR searches against both the Company and Harbourglass.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertible notes, SAFEs, ESOP awards or other rights to shares.
- **Completion deliverables:** share certificates, signed transfers, waivers of pre-emption rights, and releases of any security over the shares.
- **Warranties:** full title and capitalisation warranties as fundamental warranties (see item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). Lower risk, but tidy up.
- **Lease:** make giving the required notice to the landlord a Seller pre-Completion obligation or a Completion deliverable. Obtain a copy of the notice.
- **Mossvale:** the restriction applies to assignment, not change of control. Obtain a warranty that, apart from Bluefen and Riverlark, no Material Contract contains a change-of-control or similar trigger. We will also verify this in our own review of DD-009.
